title: Sidecar areas outside the repo and their cleanup
summary: One known home outside the repo for worktrees, scratch, test temp, walk-throughs and archives, with checked moves and measured retention.
why: Heavy output inside a repo or in system Temp bloats backups, slows logons and hides secrets; most single-repo users never need it, so the areas stay off until they do, while the outside-writes register and the runtime reaper stay on.

items.title: Sidecar root with fixed areas per repo
items.does: Sets one sidecar root for this repo outside the repo folder, with five fixed areas (Worktree, Scratch, Temp, Walk, Archive), records it in local git config and adds a rule and a small tool that prints the paths.
items.why: Repos stay small and backups stay lean when heavy output has one known home outside the repo; every worktree of the repo resolves to the same root.
items.notes: Enable later: when worktrees, evidence or bundles start to bloat the repo or Temp (replaces conv-sidecar-root).

items.title: Worktree area: lanes and adopt copies
items.does: Puts lane and adopt worktrees in the sidecar Worktree area and adds a removal check: merged into its base, clean, not locked, ignored files listed, unmerged commits saved under a ref before removal.
items.why: Worktrees and branches pile up by the dozen when nothing checks them, and some held commits that existed nowhere else; a checked removal clears the pile without losing work.
items.notes: Enable later: when you run parallel lanes or adopt copies in worktrees.

items.title: Scratch area for heavy evidence and copies
items.does: Adds a rule that measurement output, adversary copies, bundles and harness output go to the sidecar Scratch area, one folder per run.
items.why: In-repo work folders grew to hundreds of megabytes with no cleanup, and a private key was once found in shared scratch; a known per-run folder is easy to scan and to clean.
items.notes: Enable later: when measurement output or bundles start landing in the repo or in Temp.

items.title: Per-repo temp root for test runs
items.does: Adds a rule that test temp goes to a per-checkout folder in the sidecar Temp area, never the session scratchpad and never a temp root shared by two runs.
items.why: Two concurrent runs sharing one temp root broke each other, and tens of thousands of leftover temp files slowed every logon by minutes.
items.notes: Enable later: when several test runs share the machine or system Temp keeps growing.

items.title: Walk area for sandbox and walk-through harnesses
items.does: Adds a rule that sandbox configs, mapped folders and walk-through results live in the sidecar Walk area, one folder per run.
items.why: Sandbox harnesses kept in Temp were swept by a cleanup while they were still running.
items.notes: Enable later: when you run Windows Sandbox or other walk-through harnesses.

items.title: Archive area: verified bundles and zips
items.does: Adds a rule that pre-rewrite git bundles, retired copies and adopt originals go to the sidecar Archive area with their sha256 recorded and the bundle verified.
items.why: An archive nobody verified is not a backup; recording the hash and verifying the bundle at write time is the only proof it can be restored.
items.notes: Enable later: before the first history rewrite or before retiring a copy of the repo.

items.title: Move protocol: copy, compare, recycle, HOLD on consumer
items.does: Adds tools/sidecar_move.py: it holds when a tracked file still names the source, copies without following links, compares count, bytes and sha256, proves the Recycle Bin can take the source, then recycles it.
items.why: A very large copy was once deleted permanently because the bin cap was cached and a no-confirmation flag hid the warning; every step here exists to make a move impossible to lose.
items.notes: Enable later: when you start moving folders out of the repo or Temp into sidecar areas.

items.title: Retention per sidecar area
items.does: Adds tools/sidecar_reap.py: a dry run by default, an age histogram per area, and recycling of per-run folders older than a retention measured from that histogram; Archive is never cleaned automatically.
items.why: Without a retention every area grows by gigabytes; a measured retention avoids a guess that deletes too much or nothing, and a folder still named by a tracked file is kept.
items.notes: Enable later: once the sidecar areas hold enough runs to measure an age histogram.

items.title: Register of everything written outside the repo
items.does: Creates a register file that lists every path the repo writes outside its own folder, why and how it is cleaned, and a rule to update it in the same change that adds a path.
items.why: Outside writes were found only by surveys, long after they had grown; a register written at the time of the change keeps every outside path known and cleanable.

items.title: In-repo runtime dir gitignored and reaped
items.does: Gitignores a .runtime folder and log files and adds tools/reap_runtime.py, which removes regenerable runtime files past a measured age and keeps the folder under a 100 MB cap.
items.why: Spawn logs, run journals and runtime folders grew without limit into gigabytes; every file that only grows needs a reaper from the day it is created.
